text: The instance requires both summands to be nondegenerate. Pairing a product vector with (x,0) and (0,y) then forces each radical component to vanish, so the product is nondegenerate. This is the orthogonal sum of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); neither positive definiteness nor unimodularity is required. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L376) passes.
Nondegeneracy is equivalent to nondegeneracy of both factors.

The product norm is the sum of the two integral norms. Even summands therefore give an even sum; evaluating at (x,0) and (0,y) proves the converse. This matches evenness in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), including degenerate forms and zero-rank summands. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L277) passes.
The integral norm is the sum of the component norms.

The carrier is L×M inside V×W, and the pairing is B_L(x,x′)+B_M(y,y′), so the factors are orthogonal. Products preserve full finite integral carriers, giving the orthogonal sum in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Degenerate forms are allowed; the construction does not silently impose nondegeneracy. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L289) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L313) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L295) passes.
The rank is additive.
The signed determinant is multiplicative.
Product bases have the block-diagonal Gram matrix.

A vector annihilates the whole product exactly when each component annihilates its own factor: test the two coordinate inclusions. Thus nondegeneracy of the actual sum form is equivalent to both component conditions, consistent with [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). No definiteness assumption is needed. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L390) passes.
The radical is the product of the component radicals.

The negative inertia indices add under orthogonal sum. Negative definite subspaces give the lower bound; the positive, null and negative dimension identity forces equality. Lean supplies finite dimension from each full lattice and uses [the inertia-index definition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65). Degenerate summands and zero dimension remain valid. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L428) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L390) passes.
All three signature slots add componentwise.
The null directions remain the product radical.

The positive inertia indices add under orthogonal sum. Products of positive definite subspaces give the lower bound; the dimension identity and product radical give equality. This is precisely [the inertia-index definition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Signature.lean#L65) on the block-diagonal form. Full lattices supply finite dimension; degeneracy is permitted. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L428) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L390) passes.
All three signature slots add componentwise.
The null directions remain the product radical.

The map (x,y)↦(f(x),g(y)) is a rational linear equivalence preserving both the summed pairing and the product carrier. It matches [the pinned quadratic-product construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Prod.lean#L53) with the additional integral-carrier condition of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Both inputs are actual lattice isometries; no bare module equivalence is promoted to one. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L464) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L470) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L480) passes.
The ambient map acts componentwise.
The restricted map respects the first carrier inclusion.
The restricted map respects the second carrier inclusion.

Evaluating the summed integral pairing twice on the same vector gives n_L(x)+n_M(y). This agrees with the square-length convention of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3) and [the pinned quadratic-product construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Prod.lean#L53). integralNorm means B(x,x), not its half; no evenness or nonnegativity is assumed. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L238) passes.
The full integral pairing splits into the two pairings.

For the block-diagonal ambient form, left and right kernels vanish exactly when the corresponding kernels of both factors vanish. The proof tests (x,0) and (0,y) in each argument, matching nondegeneracy in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Nondegeneracy is kept distinct from anisotropy. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L390) passes.
For these symmetric forms, the radical is componentwise.

The basis is indexed by I⊕J: left basis vectors become (eᵢ,0), and right ones become (0,fⱼ). Transport along the canonical carrier equivalence gives exactly [the pinned product-basis construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Prod.lean#L38). This is a disjoint union of index types, not their Cartesian product; empty bases are allowed. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L224) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L231) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L295) passes.
Left basis vectors are included in the first factor.
Right basis vectors are included in the second factor.
The resulting Gram matrix is block diagonal.

At a left index, the product basis is the first carrier inclusion of eᵢ. This is the left-coordinate formula of [the pinned product-basis construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Prod.lean#L38); it carries no contribution from the second basis. The statement requires an actual i, so an empty left index type causes no exception. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L295) passes.
The product-basis matrix has the intended diagonal blocks and zero cross blocks.

At a right index, the product basis is the second carrier inclusion of fⱼ. This is the right-coordinate formula of [the pinned product-basis construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Prod.lean#L38), with zero first component. Index order and the actual inclusion agree; no finite or nonempty index assumption is added. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L295) passes.
The product-basis matrix has the intended diagonal blocks and zero cross blocks.

The equivalence sends a pair belonging to the product submodule to its two carrier subtypes, and pairs them back in the inverse direction. It is ℤ-linear and canonical, supplying the carrier product in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). This declaration asserts a module equivalence; preservation of forms is proved separately. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L259) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L210) passes.
The form-preserving enhancement has exactly this underlying map.
The projections and inclusions reconstruct every carrier vector.

The canonical carrier equivalence sends the first inclusion of a to (a,0). Both sides retain the same carrier element, as in the coordinate construction underlying [the pinned product-basis construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Prod.lean#L38). This is an equality of subtype elements, with no choice of representatives. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L180) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L190) passes.
Projection after the first inclusion is the identity.
The other projection is zero.

The canonical carrier equivalence sends the second inclusion of b to (0,b). This is the second-coordinate construction underlying [the pinned product-basis construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Prod.lean#L38). The zero belongs to the first carrier and b to the second, so the order of the factors is correct. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L195) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L185) passes.
Projection after the second inclusion is the identity.
The other projection is zero.

The form pairs (x,y) with (x′,y′) by B_L(x,x′)+B_M(y,y′). The coordinate copies therefore pair to zero, exactly the orthogonal sum in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); its diagonal specializes to [the pinned quadratic-product construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Prod.lean#L53). This is a sum of pairings, not their product. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L66) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L295) passes.
Evaluation is the sum of component pairings.
The Gram matrix has zero cross blocks.

The displayed formula expands the two pulled-back bilinear forms: first coordinates pair in L and second coordinates in M, then add. It is exactly the orthogonal pairing of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). The equation holds for arbitrary ambient vectors, not just integral carrier points. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L295) passes.
The formula yields the two Gram blocks and zero mixed blocks.

Taking B(p,p) in the block-diagonal form yields Q_L(x)+Q_M(y), precisely [the pinned quadratic-product construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Prod.lean#L53). The quadratic product uses addition of values. No factor of one-half appears: this is the diagonal quadratic map, not the even lattice half-norm. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L277) passes.
On carrier vectors the same identity holds integrally.

The map takes a product-carrier vector to its first carrier coordinate. The membership proof guarantees that this lies in L, and the map is ℤ-linear. This is the usual first projection for the carrier product in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); it is not asserted to preserve the full norm. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L180) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L185) passes.
First projection after first inclusion is identity.
First projection after second inclusion is zero.

Evaluation agrees with the first coordinate after the canonical carrier-product equivalence. Thus the projection acts on the actual carrier subtype, with no basis or representative choice. It is the first-coordinate map in the direct sum of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L210) passes.
The two coordinate projections reconstruct the original carrier vector.

The inclusion sends a∈L to (a,0) in the product carrier and is ℤ-linear. Zero belongs to M, so membership is valid without extra hypotheses. This is the canonical first summand embedding of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3) and the coordinate inclusion in [the pinned quadratic-product construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Prod.lean#L53). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L180) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L190) passes.
First projection is a left inverse.
The second component is zero.

The inclusion sends b∈M to (0,b) in the product carrier and is ℤ-linear. The zero first coordinate lies in L. This is the canonical second summand embedding of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3) and [the pinned quadratic-product construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Prod.lean#L53), including when either ambient space has dimension zero. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L195) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L185) passes.
Second projection is a left inverse.
The first component is zero.

The map takes a product-carrier vector to its second carrier coordinate. Carrier membership makes the codomain M correct, and the map is ℤ-linear. This is the second projection for the direct sum of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); preservation of the entire product norm is not claimed. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L195) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L190) passes.
Second projection after second inclusion is identity.
Second projection after first inclusion is zero.

Evaluation agrees with the second coordinate after the canonical carrier-product equivalence. The result is an element of M itself, with its existing membership proof. This is the second-coordinate map for the direct sum of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); no basis choice enters. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L210) passes.
The two coordinate projections reconstruct the original carrier vector.

The underlying ℤ-submodule is precisely L.carrier.prod M.carrier inside V×W. Membership therefore requires membership in each component. This is the external direct-sum carrier of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), valid even for degenerate forms; it is not a sum of submodules in one shared ambient space. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L210) passes.
Every product-carrier vector decomposes into the two canonical inclusions.

The ambient form stored in the lattice is exactly orthogonalSumForm, so it pairs coordinates separately and adds. This agrees with the orthogonal-sum convention of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3) and the diagonal quadratic construction [the pinned quadratic-product construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Prod.lean#L53). The equation concerns the rational form, not merely its integer-valued restriction. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L66) passes.
The stored form has the intended coordinate formula.

Forgetting the membership proof from the first component of the carrier equivalence gives the first ambient coordinate of p. This is the canonical product identification in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). The coercions only forget proofs; no scalar extension or additional map changes the vector. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L180) passes.
The first coordinate recovers an included first-factor vector.

Forgetting the membership proof from the second component of the carrier equivalence gives the second ambient coordinate of p. This matches the product identification in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). The target is W and the second factor is retained, with no interchange of the two carriers. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L195) passes.
The second coordinate recovers an included second-factor vector.

The integer-valued pairing on the product carrier equals the sum of the two integer-valued component pairings. Casting to ℚ gives the defining block-diagonal formula, and injectivity of ℤ→ℚ gives this equality. Thus the actual integral form agrees with the orthogonal sum in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L259) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Orthogonal/Sum.lean#L277) passes.
The carrier-product form isometry uses the canonical product map.
Diagonal evaluation gives the corresponding integral norm identity.

After coercing to V×W, the first carrier inclusion is exactly a↦(a,0). This is the coordinate inclusion of [the pinned quadratic-product construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Prod.lean#L53) and the direct-sum convention of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). The equality retains the original vector and requires no chosen basis. Compared with [Proposition7.3, pp.40–41](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Clopen.lean#L39).

Enlarging the ambient subset from F to G enlarges the connected component through the same point. When x∈F, inclusion carries its connected component into the component in G. When x∉F, Lean’s relative component is empty and the inclusion remains true. Compared with [Lemma5.7.3(3), maximality applied to subspaces](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/004T); [Lemma5.7.2, continuous inclusion](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0376) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Basic.lean#L667).

A family of preconnected subsets with nonempty total intersection has preconnected union. A point in the intersection is common to every member, so a separation of the union cannot place members on different sides. This is the connected-fan argument, with preconnectedness allowing an empty union. Compared with [Theorem4.6, p.26](https://legacy-www.math.harvard.edu/~ctm/papers/home/text/class/harvard/131/course/course.pdf); [Proof of Lemma5.7.3, common-point union argument](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/004T) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Basic.lean#L116).

A connected subset defines a connected space when equipped with its subtype topology. The source transfers preconnectedness through the inclusion and separately transfers the subset’s nonemptiness to Nonempty s. Thus the class has exactly the standard intrinsic subspace meaning. Compared with [Discussion after Remark7.4, p.41, connected subsets use the subspace topology](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [Definition5.7.1, nonempty connectedness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/004S) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Basic.lean#L804).

Connectedness of a subset is equivalent to ConnectedSpace on its subtype with the induced topology. The source preserves both parts of the notion: preconnectedness and existence of a point. In particular, an empty subset fails both sides under this convention. Compared with [Discussion after Remark7.4, p.41, subspace interpretation](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [Definition5.7.1, explicit nonemptiness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/004S) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Basic.lean#L811).

A subset is preconnected exactly when its subtype is a PreconnectedSpace. Relative open separations correspond to ambient opens intersected with the subset; the source implements this using the induced inclusion topology and continuous images. Both sides allow the empty subset. Compared with [Proposition7.3 and subspace convention, pp.40–41](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Basic.lean#L807).

Group is a monoid with a specified left inverse for every element. In an associative monoid this yields two-sided inverses, so the presentation agrees with the usual group definition. Division and integer powers are constrained to their standard interpretations. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Defs.lean#L33).

CommGroup adds commutativity to Group, giving exactly an abelian group in multiplicative notation. The identity and inverse operations remain those of the inherited group. No order, torsion restriction or nontriviality condition is imposed. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Defs.lean#L116).

AddGroup is the usual group structure written additively: an additive monoid with −a+a=0 for every a. Associativity makes the inverse two-sided. Additive notation does not impose commutativity; subtraction is constrained to a+(−b). Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Defs.lean#L44).

AddCommGroup is an additive group with commutative addition. It models an abelian group without requiring a scalar field, topology or norm. Zero, negation and subtraction are the inherited group operations. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Defs.lean#L111).

Units bundles an element of a monoid with a two-sided inverse. Both inverse equations are required, which matters in noncommutative monoids. Although the inverse is stored explicitly, uniqueness ensures that equal underlying values give equal units. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Units/Defs.lean#L49).

The units of any monoid form a group. Multiplication uses the ambient product, inversion swaps the stored value and inverse, and the identity is the ambient identity. No commutativity or invertibility of all ambient elements is required. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Units/Defs.lean#L260).

Units of a commutative monoid form a commutative group. Their multiplication is the ambient multiplication, so its commutativity transfers directly. Only the invertible elements are included; the ambient monoid itself need not be a group. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Units/Defs.lean#L266).

The inverse of a bundled unit is obtained by exchanging its value and inverse, along with the two inverse proofs. This works in every monoid, even when there is no inverse operation on the ambient type. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Units/Defs.lean#L94).

Units inherit a monoid structure from the ambient monoid. The product’s inverse is the reverse product of the supplied inverses, and natural powers have the expected underlying values. Associativity and identity laws follow through unit extensionality. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Units/Defs.lean#L228).

Units.mk0 embeds a nonzero element of a group with zero as a unit, using its supplied inverse. The nonzero hypothesis is essential: the absorbing zero cannot be a unit because zero and one are distinct. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Units/Basic.lean#L210).

Multiplying the value of a unit by the value of its inverse gives the monoid identity. The inverse here belongs to the unit group; no inverse operation on the ambient monoid is assumed. The order of the two factors matches the stored right-inverse law. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Units/Defs.lean#L201).

The value of the inverse unit multiplied by the unit’s value is the monoid identity. This is the stored left-inverse equation. It holds in noncommutative monoids and uses no globally defined ambient inversion. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Units/Defs.lean#L197).

GroupWithZero is a nontrivial monoid with absorbing zero in which every nonzero element is invertible, with 0⁻¹ fixed to zero. It agrees with the multiplicative structure of a division ring while requiring no addition or commutativity. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L216).

CommGroupWithZero adds commutativity to a group with zero. Thus the nonzero elements form an abelian multiplicative group, while zero is absorbing and has inverse zero. The structure includes no addition, so it is weaker than a field or semifield. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L240).

DivisionMonoid records involutive inversion, reversal of products under inversion, and identification of a right inverse when a product equals one. It is an auxiliary common structure for groups and groups with zero, and does not require every element to be invertible. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/DivInvMonoid.lean#L316).

DivisionCommMonoid is a commutative DivisionMonoid. Commutativity does not turn its inversion into a genuine inverse for every element: groups with zero are still included. The class adds neither addition nor a distinguished zero. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/DivInvMonoid.lean#L351).

DivInvMonoid supplies a monoid, inversion, division as a·b⁻¹, and integer powers with the prescribed zero, natural-successor and negative-successor rules. It imposes no inverse-cancellation law. This is deliberate support for weaker pseudo-inverse operations. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/DivInvMonoid.lean#L145).

ZPow is the implementation carrier for an integer-power operation, storing a function ℤ→G→G. Its own class documentation identifies this role. It carries no power laws or multiplication structure; DivInvMonoid supplies the recursion requirements. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/DivInvMonoid.lean#L116).

If a·b=1 in a DivisionMonoid, then b is the supplied inverse of a. This is exactly the class’s inverse-identification property with the equality reversed. It does not infer that arbitrary elements have inverses. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Basic.lean#L368).

Dividing a by b⁻¹ equals a·b because division multiplies on the right by the inverse and inversion is involutive. No nonzero condition is needed. In a group with zero, b=0 gives zero on both sides. Compared with [the reference](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Basic.lean#L508).
